scope: Shared named palette library, manual and prompt creation, management, detached workflow application and palette-guided generated-source revisions.
artist_task: Define a color collection once, refine its colors/order, and reuse it in different layers and sketches.
computation_removed: Repeated RGB entry and prompt formatting. This is app orchestration around existing palette inputs; no new portable algorithm or corpus recreation claim.
semantics: Named snapshots contain 2–12 ordered opaque RGB hex colors, matching existing workflow bounds. Duplicate colors and ordering are meaningful and retained.
Manual color/hex editing, reorder, add/remove, rename, duplicate and delete; prompt output remains an editable unsaved draft until explicit save.
Atomic JSON storage under harness/palettes. Revision checks reject stale edits/deletes. Existing sketches own detached color values and do not change when a library record changes.
Studio workflow Style controls and gallery study controls share the picker. Applying a palette is one undoable edit and preserves the other layer inputs.

Studio generated-layer shortcut prepares edit scope and selected palette; artist generates/reviews/applies using the existing candidate flow. Studio and Explorations generation can include chosen exact RGB values.
Palette dialog is portaled outside responsive drawers, with bounded scrolling and native modal focus/Escape behavior.

Final integration connects the six existing expansion workflows to their already reviewed adapters in the harness compositor, correcting a missing dispatch found by the full browser suite. No operation semantics changed.

validation.unit_tests: 52/52 passed; palette persistence, detached values, concurrent-edit/deletion conflicts, invalid names/colors/count, model response validation and abort propagation included.
validation.build: Final production Next build and TypeScript passed. Existing jobs.ts filesystem tracing warning remains.

request.prompt: A muted coastal palette: deep ink blue, sea-glass green, pale seafoam, warm sand, and a small coral accent. Avoid neon colors.

source_revision.initial_outcome: Model returned placeholder candidate id pending without source or render. Candidate validation rejected it; no artwork accepted.
source_revision.retry_prompt:
Use this ordered color palette for the artwork: #1b3a57, #7a9e9f, #d4e5e2, #d9c7a9, #d98a7e. Preserve the requested structure; use these exact RGB colors as the base colors.

Recolor the selected source layer: use sea-glass green #7a9e9f for the central disk and ink blue #1b3a57 for its twelve rings. Preserve the ring count, geometry, layout, seeds, transparency, and diskRadius control. Keep the same layer id. Use candidate.create with the full revised files, render the candidate, and return the real candidate id from that tool. Do not return a placeholder or claim completion without a rendered candidate.
source_revision.result: Root inspected exact before/after source: only fill/stroke RGB and comments changed. Twelve rings, diskRadius, geometry, replay inputs and transparency preserved. Native 640px image has the requested disk RGB #7a9e9f; source stroke is #1b3a57.

application.transport: Completed real source-revision run replayed; candidate validation/application, artifact loading, canvas composition and undo/redo live.
application.pixel_check: Final live browser waited for center pixel RGB (122,158,159) after redo before capturing.

validation.visual_review: Root inspected library, manual/prompt editors, mobile modal, exact source diff, native raster and final applied Studio canvas.

limits: Palette library is shared within this trusted local installation. Browser-only offline palette management is not implemented; existing direct workflow color controls remain local.
Generated source uses model-driven revisions, not deterministic recoloring. One palette creation and one successful retry do not establish general prompt quality.

Browser generation tests replay completed responses or intercept requests. Live model generation/native rendering and live browser candidate application were checked separately; no uninterrupted browser-to-model claim.
No portable operation, new target acceptance or corpus recreation coverage is added.
